subject: Weekly AI-in-CIMs scan - 17 ingested, 9 with signal
body:
This is the weekly AI-in-CIMs scan. It reads every CIM ingested into the Knowledge Vault for how the seller substantiates AI claims - underwritten in the numbers versus positioned as capability - and turns what sellers are figuring out into questions for specific WCP portcos.

Window: 17 CIMs ingested since the last digest (Aug 28). Twelve arrived in one batch through the DealCloud migration folder, so several are older documents newly ingested rather than fresh deal flow - one is a November 2024 CIP. The claim is about ingestion, not origination. 9 produced notes. The tier scale: 4 = AI in the forecast numbers, 3 = quantified AI operations not underwritten, 2 = named products or roadmap without numbers, 1-0 = mentions or nothing.

Lead item: Marketron put AI inside the EBITDA margin bridge

Marketron (Project Amplify - broadcast advertising software, ~$26M 2026B revenue, $7.0M 2026B Adj. EBITDA) states a path to a 35.1% Adj. EBITDA margin by 2028P "driven by TaaS margin expansion, AI / automation-driven operating leverage, and continued revenue mix shift, each already in active execution." The tech-enabled services line is explicitly AI-staffed: "AI agents automate routine tasks within the hybrid onshore plus offshore workflow," with an agentic onboarding layer claimed to cut time-to-productivity per new hire. TaaS is sized as a ~$50M revenue opportunity across ~4,000 eligible stations. No third-party validation of the agent productivity claims appears in the sections reviewed.

Read: This is agentic labor underwritten into a services margin, the sharpest such claim in the corpus so far. The diligence question it teaches: how much of the 2028P margin survives if the agents deliver nothing beyond current-state productivity?

Tier 4 - AI in the numbers

Marketron Broadcast Solutions (Project Amplify) - detailed above. Relevant portcos: PracticeTek, because it runs the same vertical-SaaS-plus-payments model where a tech-enabled service tier is the next attach, and Marketron shows what bankers now accept as an AI-staffed service line story. TeamSnap, because its advertising and sponsorship revenue rides on ad-workflow tooling of exactly the kind Marketron automates. Question: which WCP vertical-software portco could underwrite an AI-staffed service tier as a forecast line today, and what evidence would we demand before crediting it in our own plans?

IHRDC (Project Eagle) - energy workforce training. Books AI as a discrete revenue line: "AI-enabled Operational Excellence Programs scaling from $0.5mm to $4.7mm" inside the PF revenue forecast to $30.0mm by 2031, alongside a named AI coaching agent (NAVAGANT) and a product vision recasting competency management as an "AI orchestration engine." The market sizing also runs on AI itself - data-center power demand argued as a driver of oil and gas training need. Relevant portcos: Career Certified, because Houlihan Lokey's AI Readiness Report for it (Jan 2026, in the Vault) shows bankers already scoring AI posture, and IHRDC is the next step - a priced AI program line. HSI, because its compliance and training content library is the same asset class IHRDC is converting into AI orchestration. Talogy, because competency models are its core IP and IHRDC licensing a client's models shows those assets trading standalone. Question: do Career Certified or HSI have a priced AI SKU anywhere in plan, or is AI still bundled invisibly into existing content - and which position does a buyer reward at exit?

Tier 3 - quantified, not underwritten

Optimy (Project Easel) - European CSR/impact SaaS, EUR 8.2M ARR 2026E. Presents an engineering AI-adoption dashboard as a diligence exhibit: 45% of committed code AI-assisted (objective 100% by early Q3), ~2 days per week of productivity gain per engineer, 100% of the team using AI daily, 70% rated advanced or expert. Names its vendor selection - Claude, after a Q4 2025 benchmark against Augment Code, Gemini and ChatGPT - plus an MCP interoperability track and an AI governance stack (ISO 27001 with AI integrated, EU AI Act mapping). The forecast runs on the ARR pipeline; no AI line in the P&L bridge. Relevant portcos: PracticeTek, TeamSnap and Science Exchange, because these are WCP's software engineering organizations and Optimy defines what a prepared seller's AI exhibit now looks like in a process. Question: if a buyer asked any WCP software portco for Optimy's four numbers today, could it produce them - and would we like the answer?

New Reach Holdco (Project Horizons) - real estate and financial education communities, $150M 2025A net revenue. Prices AI as a member-facing product rather than internal efficiency: MALLI Pro, a premium AI subscription tier with a $500K 2026 target and ~$2.0M yearly revenue expected at rollout - explicitly labeled upside to budget, not in the base case; 575 Mac Mini M4 units deployed as dedicated AI instances for flagship members; a Q4 2026 "Agentic Autonomy" milestone connecting its deal tools via MCP. Relevant portcos: Career Certified, because real estate education is its core market and this is live evidence that the customer base pays for AI as a premium tier, not a bundled feature. TeamSnap, because MALLI Pro is a pricing test case for AI tiers in a passion-community context. Question: is there a premium AI tier worth piloting at Career Certified - budgeted as upside, the way this seller had the discipline to present it?

Tier 2 - named products, no numbers

Enliven Health (Project ELGIN) - pharmacy technology. Markets an "Intelligent Orchestration Layer for Pharmacy" - next-best-action guidance and automation across adherence, refill, billing, reconciliation and outreach - with a responsible-AI frame for regulated healthcare. Notably, the 15% to 30% margin bridge is attributed to mix shift and cloud operating leverage, not AI, and a $3.5M cost right-sizing is attributed to a RIF with no AI mention. The counter-example to Marketron in the same cohort. Relevant portcos: Apotheco, because adherence, refill and outreach workflows are the daily operating work of a specialty pharmacy - Enliven is selling the orchestration layer for exactly those tasks. PromptCare, because adherence and reconciliation automation map onto specialty infusion operations. Question: has Apotheco formally answered build-vs-buy on pharmacy workflow AI, now that a category vendor is selling it?

CreditXpert - mortgage credit optimization SaaS, $25M ARR Apr-26, 109% NRR. Draws an "Agentic AI Layer" above its API stack explicitly marked "Represents Future Use Cases," with a 3Q26-2Q28 roadmap of agentic functionality and multi-LLM orchestration - while attributing all current growth to its SaaS conversion and usage-based pricing. A clean separation of priced-today versus future use case. Relevant portco: PracticeTek, because usage-based monetization of analytics modules on a contracted SaaS base is the same upsell math its payments and module attach runs on. Question: when WCP portcos present AI roadmaps to boards or buyers, do we enforce the same priced-today versus future-use-case separation - and would each portco's current deck survive that test?

Infosec Boot Camps (Project Olympus, Cengage carve-out) - cybersecurity certification training. Productizes AI as syllabus: a 5-day Generative and Agentic AI boot camp, ISACA's AAISM credential, EC-Council's Certified Offensive AI Security Pro. The certification bodies - the industry's pricing anchors - have already minted AI-security credentials. Relevant portcos: HSI, because AI-security and AI-governance credentials are the adjacent SKU class now moving in corporate L&D budgets. Career Certified, because new credentials from recognized bodies are new prep markets with built-in demand. Question: should HSI or Career Certified attach to existing AI credentials as prep and delivery partners now, rather than build proprietary AI curricula later?

Tier 0-1 - portfolio-relevant only

MedTec Healthcare & Private Duty - home care CIP (Lincoln sell-side, Nov 2024, newly ingested into the Senior Helpers / Altocare target folder): zero AI language, which is the category norm. For Altocare add-on underwriting, is that an accepted gap or a screen - a target with even basic scheduling automation is differentiated here.

ARC Medical Rehab (Project Raven) - multi-state outpatient rehab CIM (Intrepid, June 2026) with no AI story at all. Ivy Rehab's live scribe program (~$2.4-2.6M scale per Vault board materials) is ahead of anything this category is marketing - does that show up as an explicit valuation argument in Ivy's next exit materials?

Feedback: reply to this email. Replies are read before each Friday run - factual corrections are applied to the underlying notes, and the next digest opens with what changed and who flagged it.

Generated by Claude against the WCP Knowledge Vault. Portfolio inferences are agent-generated and unreviewed. Reply to Prithvi with corrections.
